Rashi on Pesachim 26b:10:1.hebrew: הא רבי - דקתני "חדש יותץ" — רבי הוא, דאמר: הפת אסורה משום דגמרה באיסור. והוא הדין לתנור חדש, שנגמר נמי ע"י האיסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:10:1.english: This is Rabbi - That which it teaches, "[A] new [oven] must be shattered," is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who said: The bread is forbidden because it was completed by [means of] a forbidden substance; and the same applies to a new oven, which was also completed by means of the forbidden substance.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:11:1.hebrew: אימור דשמעת ליה לרבי דיש שבח עצים בפת - כי שמעת ליה דפליג רבי אדרבנן, ביש שבח עצים בפת לחודא הוא דשמעת ליה — דרבנן הוו מקילי טפי ושרו אפי' פת לאכול, דאמרי: אין שבח עצים בה, אלא שבח היסק, ואיסור שבה כבר כלה הוא; ורבי סבר: הואיל ואבוקה כנגדו, יש שבח עצים ואיסור גמור בה. וגבי תנור חדש, נהי דיש שבח עצים בו, מיהו הוא עצמו אין נאכל, אלא להיסק אחר עומד ויאפו בו, ונמצאת פת הנאפת בו נגמרת ע"י איסור והיתר — עצי איסור שגמרו (בו) את התנור, ועצי היתר שגמרו את הפת. והא, היכא שמעינן ליה דאסר רבי:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:11:1.english: Say that you heard that Rabbi [holds] that there is improvement of the wood in the bread - When you heard that Rabbi disagrees with the Rabbis, it was only regarding [the principle that] there is improvement of the wood in the bread that you heard him — for the Rabbis were more lenient and permitted even the bread to be eaten, as they say: There is no improvement of the wood in it, but rather the improvement of the heat, and the prohibited item that was in it has already ceased to exist; and Rabbi maintains: Since the flame is facing it, there is improvement of the wood and absolute prohibited matter in it. And with regard to a new oven, granted that there is improvement of the wood in it, however it itself is not eaten; rather, it stands for another firing and they will bake in it, and the bread baked in it turns out to be completed through [both] the prohibited and the permitted — the prohibited wood that completed (with it) the oven, and the permitted wood that completed the bread. And this [case of "this and that cause it"] — where have we heard that Rabbi prohibits [it]?

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:11:2.hebrew: הא ר' אליעזר - דשמעינן ליה זה וזה גורם אסור — דבר שאיסור והיתר גרמו לו שיבא, אסור בהנאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:11:2.english: This is Rabbi Eliezer - For we have heard him [hold that when] both this and that cause [it], it is forbidden — [meaning that] an item that [both] a forbidden [factor] and a permitted [factor] caused to come [into being] is forbidden from benefit.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:12:2.hebrew: אחר אחרון אני בא - אם סילק את הראשון, כדמתרץ ליה אביי:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:12:2.english: I follow the last - [This applies only] if he removed the first [one], as Abaye explains it.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:1:1.english: This is not comparable - It is an answer:

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:1:2.hebrew: שכן עליה עוף - בפרה אדומה קאי, שפרח ונח על גבה. אע"ג דכתיב "לא עלה עליה עול", דמשמע "עליה" — אפילו עליה בעלמא; ואי משום דכתיב "עול", הא מרבינן ביה שאר עבודות במסכת סוטה (דף מו.) — אפ"ה בהא עלייה כשרה, דלא ניחא ליה. והוא הדין להכניסה לרבקה ודשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:1:2.english: A bird landed on it - [The Baraitha] is referring to the red heifer, where [a bird] flew and rested upon its back. Even though it is written: “upon which a yoke never came” (Numbers 19:2), which implies [from the word] “upon it” [that] even mere coming upon it [disqualifies it]; and if [you might say it is valid] because it is written “a yoke,” behold, we include other [types of] labor from it in tractate Sotah (46a) — even so, with this coming upon [it, the heifer] is valid, since it is not pleasing to him. And the same law applies to [the case of one who] brought it into the team and it threshed.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:1:3.hebrew: עלה עליה זכר פסולה - דניחא ליה, והוא הדין לתינק ותידוש:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:1:3.english: [If] a male mounted it, it is disqualified - For it is pleasing to him; and the same applies to [the case of bringing it in so] that it will nurse and thresh.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:2:1.hebrew: עובד - משמע ממילא, עבד משמע בידים. ואף על גב דהאי בעגלה כתיב — תרווייהו ילפינן מהדדי בגזרה שוה דעול עול במסכת סוטה (דף מו.):
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:2:1.english: It was worked - [This passive form] implies [labor performed] on its own, [whereas] “he worked” implies [labor performed directly] by [human] hands. And even though this [verse] is written regarding the heifer [whose neck is broken], we derive both of them from each other via a verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah] of “yoke” [and] “yoke” in tractate Sotah (46a).

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:4:1.english: He may not spread it out - [The baraita] is speaking of one who finds a lost garment.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:4:2.english: A frame - Cheville [Old French for a peg or rack].

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:4:3.english: For its own sake - So that moths will not consume it.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:4:4.hebrew: נזדמנו לו אורחין וכו' - אלמא אף על גב דלצורכה הוא — והיינו לא אפשר — הואיל ומתכוין להתכבד בשל חבירו באורחין, חשיב ליה גזל, ואסיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:4:4.english: If guests happen to come to him, etc. - Evidently, even though it is for its [own] need — and that is [a case where benefit is] unavoidable — since he intends to be honored before guests with his fellow's [property], it is considered robbery, and is forbidden.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:5:1.hebrew: ומשני - לאו משום כוונה הוא, אלא משום דבשטיחה זו קלי לה — כלומר מאבדה בידים — אי משום עינא בישא, אי משום דלמא אורחין גנבי נינהו וגנבי לה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:5:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers - It is not on account of [his] intention; rather, because in this spreading [it] out he ruins it — that is to say, he destroys it with [his own] hands — either because of the evil eye, or because perhaps the guests are thieves and will steal it.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:6:1.hebrew: מוכרין כדרכן - מעוטפין בכסות כלאים, דאין מתכוין להנאת לבישה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:6:1.english: Sell them as they normally would - Wrapped in a garment of diverse kinds, as he does not intend for the benefit of wearing [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:6:2.english: And the modest - Abstinent people who distance themselves from impropriety and from anything resembling it.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:7:1.hebrew: לישנא קמא דרבא - אפשר ולא מתכוין — אסור, אפילו לרבי שמעון; דא"כ, הא מני:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:7:1.english: The first version of Rava - [Where it is] possible [to avoid] and one does not intend [to derive benefit, it is] forbidden, even according to Rabbi Shimon; for if so, whose [view] is this?

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:7:2.hebrew: יש שטועין שמקשין על משנה זו אותה ששנינו: בגד שאבד בו כלאים לא ימכרנו לנכרי — אלמא כלאים אסור למכור. וטעות בידם, דהתם אבד דוקא — שמא יחזור נכרי וימכרנו לישראל, ולא יכיר שיש בו כלאים, וילבשנו; אבל כלאים הניכר מותר בכל הנאות מכירה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:7:2.english: There are some who err, who raise a difficulty against this mishna [from] that which we learned: 'A garment in which diverse kinds [kilayim] was lost, one may not sell it to a gentile' — which implies that it is prohibited to sell diverse kinds [kilayim]. And they are mistaken, for there, [the prohibition applies] specifically [where the kilayim was] lost, lest the gentile turn around and sell it to a Jew, who will not recognize that there is diverse kinds [kilayim] in it and will wear it; but recognizable diverse kinds [kilayim] is permitted for all benefit of sale.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:8:1.hebrew: בקליפי ערלה - קליפי אגוזים ורמונים, שאף הם בכלל פרי ואסורין משום ערלה. וכן קשין של כלאי הכרם — הכל אסור, דבכלאים לא כתיב פרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:8:1.english: With peels of orla - Peels of nuts and pomegranates, which are also included in [the category of] fruit and are forbidden under [the prohibition of] orla. And likewise, straw of diverse kinds in a vineyard — everything is forbidden, because regarding diverse kinds, “fruit” is not written.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:8:2.hebrew: חדש יותץ - שהרי על ידי היסק זה של ערלה, נגמר ומתקיים כולו:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:8:2.english: A new [oven] must be shattered - For through this firing of orlah, it is completed and made durable in its entirety.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:8:3.hebrew: ישן - שאין היסק זה מועיל לו, אלא שאופה בו פת:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:8:3.english: An old [oven] - For this heating does not benefit it, except that one bakes bread in it.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:8:4.english: It shall be cooled - So that one does not bake bread in it with this heating.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:9:1.hebrew: אפה בו פת - בהיסק זה. לקמן מוקי לה כשאבוקה כנגדו, שכל שעה שהיתה פת בתנור היה דולק האור ואופהו, שהיה נהנה מן האיסור בשעה שהאיסור בעין:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:9:1.english: [If] one baked bread in it - With this heating. Later on, [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring to a case] where the torch was opposite it, such that the entire time that the bread was in the oven, the fire was burning and baking it, so that he was benefiting from the prohibited item while the prohibited item was physically present.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:9:2.english: Rabbi says: The bread is prohibited - For there is improvement [imparted by] prohibited wood in the bread.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:9:3.hebrew: וחכמים אומרים הפת מותרת - (דהא) סברי: אין שבח עצים בפת ממש, והוא הדין דלית להו נמי חדש יותץ, אלא יוצן. והכי אמרי' בשמעתין:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:9:3.english: And the Rabbis say: The bread is permitted - [For] they hold that there is no tangible improvement of the wood in the bread; and by the same reasoning, they also do not hold [that a] new [oven] must be shattered, but rather [that] it may be cooled down. And so we say in our sugya.

Rashi on Pesachim 26b:9:4.hebrew: בישלה על גבי גחלים - דברי הכל הפת מותרת, ואפילו לרבי; דכי איתהני פת מאיסור — כבר כלה ובטל. וגחלים איצטריכא ליה, דלא תימא: אכתי איסורא בעיניה; וכל שכן בתנור גרוף ואין אבוקה כנגדו:
Rashi on Pesachim 26b:9:4.english: If he cooked it over coals - Everyone agrees that the bread is permitted, even according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]; for when the bread derives benefit from the forbidden [fuel], [the fuel] has already been consumed and nullified. And [mentioning] coals was necessary for him, so that you would not say: The forbidden substance is still [present] in its original form; and all the more so in [the case of] a swept oven where there is no flame opposite it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:10:1.hebrew: בין חדש בין ישן יוצן - דזה וזה גורם מותר. אף על גב דזה וזה גורם דוקא בדיעבד מותר — כדמוכח בסוף פרק כל הצלמים (ע"ז מח:), דאמר רבי יוסי: "אין נוטעין אגוז של ערלה", ומודה ר' יוסי שאם נטע שהוא מותר, וחשיב ליה זה וזה גורם — דהכא הוי כדיעבד, דאם נאמר "חדש יותץ", יפסיד התנור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:10:1.english: "Whether new or old, it may be cooled" - For [the Rabbis hold that when] "both this and that cause [it]," [it is] permitted. And even though "both this and that cause [it]" is permitted specifically bedi'avad [after the fact], as is proven at the end of the chapter [entitled] "Kol HaTzelamim" (Avodah Zarah 48b), where Rabbi Yose says: "One may not plant a walnut of orlah, but Rabbi Yose concedes that if he planted [it], it is permitted," and [the Gemara there] considers it [a case of] "both this and that cause [it]" — [nevertheless,] here it is considered like bedi'avad, for if we were to say "[A] new [oven] must be shattered," he would lose the oven.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:10:2.hebrew: בין חדש ובין ישן יוצן - ואף על גב דזה וזה גורם מותר, מ"מ ישן, כיון דסגי ליה בצינון ולא מפסיד מידי אלא איסור הנאה לחודה — לכך צריך צינון:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:10:2.english: "Whether [it is] new or [it is] old, it may be cooled" - And even though [when] both this and that cause [it, it is] permitted, nevertheless, [in the case of] an old [oven], since it is sufficient for it [to undergo] cooling and he does not lose anything except the forbidden benefit alone, therefore it requires cooling.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:1:1.hebrew: הא לא דמיא אלא להא שכן עליה עוף - מייתי לה משום דרב פפא אמר מילתיה עלה, לפי שהיא משנה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:1:1.english: "This is comparable only to that: A bird landed on it" - [The Gemara] cites this [Mishnah] because Rav Pappa stated his teaching regarding it, since it is a Mishnah.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:1:2.hebrew: עלה עליה זכר פסולה - וא"ת: אמאי פסולה? הא ודאי לא ניחא ליה להפסיד פרה שדמיה יקרים בשביל דבר מועט! וי"ל: דאם נאמר כשירה, הוה ניחא ליה, ולכך אין להכשירה. וא"ת: הכניסה לרבקה ודשה, אמאי כשירה? מ"ש מעלה עליה זכר דפסולה? וי"ל: דהתם לא ניחא ליה בדישתה, שאין מרויח כלום בדישתה, דבלאו הכי נידושה התבואה. וה"ר יהודה פירש, דסתם פרה בחורה היא, ומסתמא אין אדם רוצה להטריחה. וא"ת: והא דתנן: "פרה מעוברת, ר' אליעזר מכשיר וחכמים פוסלין", והכא אמר: "עלה עליה זכר פסולה"? וי"ל: דהכא כחכמים דפוסלין; דה"נ ר' יהודה פליג ואמר: דוקא העלה עליה זכר, אבל עלה מעצמו — כשירה. אי נמי, הא דאמר הכא "פסולה", היינו כשרואה בשעת עלייה וניחא ליה, כדאמר גבי הכשר (בפ"ק דחולין) (דף יג.): "עודהו הטל עליהן ושמח — הרי זה בכי יותן; נגבו — אינן בכי יותן", דבעינן "יותן" דומיא ד"יתן", אף על פי שאם היה יודע בעוד הטל עליהן היה שמח. והא דאמרינן בפרק עגלה ערופה (סוטה מו.): "עול פוסל בין בשעת עבודה ובין שלא בשעת עבודה, שאר דברים אינן פוסלין אלא בשעת עבודה" — מה שהזכר משמש בה חשוב עבודה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:1:2.english: [If] a male mounted it, it is disqualified - And if you say: Why is it disqualified? Surely he certainly does not find it pleasing to ruin a heifer whose value is high for the sake of a minor benefit! And one can say: For if we were to say it is valid, it would indeed be pleasing to him, and therefore it cannot be validated. And if you say: [If] he brought it into a team [of thresher cattle] and it threshed, why is it valid? How is this different from [the case where] a male mounted it, where it is disqualified? And one can say: There, he does not find its threshing pleasing, as he gains nothing from its threshing, since the grain would be threshed anyway without it. And Harav Rabbi Yehudah explained that an ordinary heifer is young, and presumably a person does not wish to overwork it. And if you say: But what about that which we learned in a Mishnah: "[Regarding] a pregnant heifer, Rabbi Eliezer validates [it] and the Sages disqualify [it]," whereas here it says: "[If] a male mounted it, it is disqualified"? And one can say: Here [the baraita is] in accordance with the Sages, who disqualify [it]; for so too, Rabbi Yehudah disagrees and says: Specifically [if] he caused a male to mount it [is it disqualified], but [if it] mounted on its own, it is valid. Alternatively, that which it says here, "it is disqualified," is when he sees [it] at the time of mounting and it is pleasing to him — as [the Gemara] says regarding [produce being rendered] susceptible [to ritual impurity] in the first chapter of Chullin (13a): "[If] dew was still upon them and he rejoiced, this is [subject to the rule of] 'if it be put' (ki yutan); [if] they dried, they are not [subject to the rule of] 'if it be put'," for we require that "it be put" [must be] similar to "he puts," even though had he known while the dew was still upon them he would have rejoiced. And as for that which we say in the chapter [entitled] Eglah Arufah (Sotah 46a): "A yoke disqualifies whether at the time of labor or not at the time of labor, [whereas] other things disqualify only at the time of labor" — the fact that the male mates with it is considered labor.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:4:1.hebrew: מגוד - פירש ר"ת: כמו נגוד ליה גלימא (עירובין ד' צד.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:4:1.english: “A frame” - Rabbeinu Tam explained [that this is] like “spread a cloak for it” (Eruvin 94a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:8:1.hebrew: חדש יותץ - קסבר: יש שבח עצים בפת, וה"נ יש שבח עצים בתנור, וזה וזה גורם — אסור. ויש שבח עצים בפת — היינו העצים שהן גורמים אפיית הפת כשאבוקה כנגדו. ורבנן סברי: אין שבח עצים בפת, אף על פי שהאבוקה כנגדו; דשלהבת אינה באה מן העצים, אלא מחמת משהו הנשרף, וא"כ היא כמו גחלת, דאין האיסור בעין. וכן פירש"י. הקשה ה"ר אהרן לרבי: הא דאמר (תרומות פ"ב מ"ג) "המבשל בשבת בשוגג יאכל" — ואפילו בשבת — ואמאי? נימא: יש שבח מוקצה בפת, דגחלים מוקנין הן! ואומר ר"י: דלא שייך אלא באיסורי הנאה דווקא. וכן פי' הקונטרס בפרק בתרא דע"ז (דף סו. ושם) גבי תנור שהסיקו בכמון של תרומה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:8:1.english: A new [oven] must be shattered - [The Tanna] maintains: There is enhancement of the wood in the bread, and so too, there is enhancement of the wood in the oven, and [benefit resulting from] "this and that causes" is forbidden. And [when it states that] "there is enhancement of the wood in the bread," that refers to wood that causes the baking of the bread when the flame is opposite it. And the Rabbis maintain: There is no enhancement of the wood in the bread, even though the flame is opposite it; for the flame does not come [directly] from the wood, but rather by virtue of something being consumed, and if so, it is like a coal, where the forbidden substance is not present in its original form. And so Rashi explained. Rabbi Aaron raised an objection to Rabbi: Concerning that which [the Mishnah] states (Terumot 2:3), "One who cooks on Shabbat unwittingly may eat [the food]" — and [this applies] even on Shabbat [itself] — why? Let us say that there is enhancement of muktzeh in the bread, for coals are muktzeh! And the Ri says: [This principle] applies only to items forbidden from benefit specifically. And so Rashi explained in the final chapter of Avodah Zarah (66a, and see there) regarding an oven that one fueled with cumin of terumah.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:9:1.hebrew: בישלה על גבי גחלים - בישלה — דווקא בדיעבד; אף על גב דכל הנשרפין אפרן מותר אפילו לכתחלה, יש לחלק בין אפרן לגחלים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26b:9:1.english: "If he cooked it over coals" - [The baraita states] "If he cooked it" [to indicate that it is permitted] specifically after the fact. Even though [with regard to] all things that are to be burned, their ash is permitted even ab initio, one must distinguish between their ash and coals.
